correctness.rationale: Algebraic gcds give gcd(a,b)=2 exactly when n=2(mod4), gcd(b,c)=2 exactly when n=1(mod4), gcd(a,c)=gcd(2n+1,3m+8). For odd m>=3, all three are minimal. The classical dimension-three gluing criterion reduces symmetry to explicit pair memberships; for nonadjacent pair d, s=(2n+1)/d, a/d>n for s>=3 and the q-positive/q-negative inequalities exclude all representations, while s=1 gives b=(n+1)a/t+n c/t. Adjacent gcd-two pairs yield exactly low n=2 and odd m in {3,5,7}, apart from m9 already covered by t|K. The residue decomposition of glued semigroups proves the Frobenius formulas and symmetric genus. Standalone exact-gcd enumerations (198602 pairs) and separately computed Apéry genus/Frobenius comparisons (624 pairs) produced VERIFY_OK. Finite tests support, rather than substitute for, the universal proof.
